# Employees incorrectly treated as independent contractors

See penalties and charges if you incorrectly treat an employee as a contractor, and how to report such a business.

**Last updated** 29 August 2025

Print or Download

## On this page

- [Penalties and charges](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/employee-or-independent-contractor/employees-incorrectly-treated-as-independent-contractors#ato-Penaltiesandcharges)
- [How to report a business](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/employee-or-independent-contractor/employees-incorrectly-treated-as-independent-contractors#ato-Howtoreportabusiness)

## Penalties and charges

Businesses who incorrectly treat an employee as an independent contractor risk receiving penalties and charges, including:

- [PAYG withholding penalty](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/paying-the-ato/interest-and-penalties/penalties/failure-to-withhold) for failing to deduct tax from worker payments and send it to the ATO
- [super guarantee charge](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/super-for-employers/quarterly-super-to-30-june-2026/missed-and-late-super-guarantee-payments/the-super-guarantee-charge)(SGC), which is more than the super that would have been paid if the worker was classified correctly. SGC consists of:

  - super guarantee shortfall amount
  - nominal interest
  - an administration fee
- additional [super guarantee penalties](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/super-for-employers/quarterly-super-to-30-june-2026/missed-and-late-super-guarantee-payments/super-guarantee-penalties) including the Part 7 penalty amount of up to 200% of the SGC under the _Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992_.

[Sham contracting - Fair Work OmbudsmanExternal Link](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/find-help-for/independent-contractors/sham-contracting) is a contravention under the _Fair Work Act 2009_. Courts can impose penalties against a business or person that incorrectly tells an employee they are an independent contractor, when in fact they're an employee of the business.

For more information, see:

- [Employee or independent contractor](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/employee-or-independent-contractor)
- [What to do if a worker wants to be an independent contractor](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/employee-or-independent-contractor/employees-incorrectly-treated-as-independent-contractors/what-to-do-if-a-worker-wants-to-be-a-independent-contractor)

## How to report a business

If you know or suspect a business is incorrectly treating an employee as an independent contractor, let us know by [Making a tip-off](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/tax-avoidance/the-fight-against-tax-crime/what-you-can-do/making-a-tip-off).

[**What to do if a worker wants to be a independent contractor**](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/employee-or-independent-contractor/employees-incorrectly-treated-as-independent-contractors/what-to-do-if-a-worker-wants-to-be-a-independent-contractor)

Find out what to do if a worker demands to be treated as an independent contractor, even though they are an employee.
